  "text": "On Monday Mara collected the things from the ward. The nurse brought them in a white plastic bag with a space for a name, though nobody had written one. Inside were slippers, a washbag and the cardigan Mara had taken in on Saturday. One sleeve was still turned inside out.

'Is there any jewellery?' Mara asked.

The nurse checked a cupboard. While she waited, Mara looked at the notice about parking charges. She had bought a weekly ticket that morning.

Her mother's wedding ring came in a small envelope. Mara put it in the zipped pocket of her handbag, where she kept foreign coins.

Outside, her brother was moving his car from a space reserved for ambulances. He lowered the passenger window.

'Did you get everything?'

She held up the bag.

'I can take that,' he said.

'It's all right.'

He had to collect his daughter. They agreed to speak later, then stood for a moment on either side of the open window, neither seeming sure who should move first.

At home Mara washed the cardigan with two work shirts. She checked the label twice and chose the cooler setting. The slippers she left in the bag by the washing machine.

On Wednesday her brother sent her a photograph of a gas meter and asked whether she knew which figures mattered. She enlarged it with her fingers. There was a strip of her mother's kitchen wallpaper above the meter, yellow flowers behind the pipes.

'Not the red ones,' she wrote.

Then she asked if he had found the stopcock. He didn't reply."
